status_summary: No DHS directive or program reinvigorating or expanding enforcement against Chinese e-commerce sellers, shippers or warehouse operators over counterfeit goods was found. A trade-press report dated 2026-04-07 on CBP's fiscal year 2025 figures says intellectual property seizures rose to 25,079 from 20,516 in fiscal year 2024 (22.2 percent), with a retail value of about 7.4 billion dollars against 5.5 billion dollars; CBP lists a fiscal year 2025 seizure statistics report, whose China and e-commerce breakdown was not read. The suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment, tracked in c26-03, subjects low-value parcels to formal entry and is context only.
title: Expand DHS enforcement against Chinese e-commerce sellers and shippers of counterfeits
uncertainties: CBP pages, including the fiscal year 2025 statistics report and a CBP release on enforcing the end of de minimis seen only as a search result, could not be fetched, so the seizure figures rest on one trade-press report and are not counted as an event. A rise in seizures does not show a policy change or a China focus. Searches of DHS, CBP, ICE and White House sites for a 2025 or 2026 e-commerce counterfeit directive returned only first-term era items. This is a judgment call: a reader who counts the de minimis suspension as an expanded crackdown on e-commerce shipments could stage the record in_progress, but that action is tariff policy tracked in c26-03.
